arxiv-2012-03042.title: The energy-momentum tensor at the earliest stage of relativistic heavy-ion collisions
arxiv-2012-03042.creator: Margaret E. Carrington, Alina Czajka, Stanisław Mrówczyński
arxiv-2012-03042.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Margaret E. Carrington, Alina Czajka, Stanisław Mrówczyński. Nuclear collisions at high energies produce a gluon field that can be described using the Colour Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory at proper times τ ≲ 1 \tau\lesssim 1 fm. The theory can be used to calculate the gluon energy-momentum tensor, which provides information about the early time evolution of the chromo-electric and chromo-magnetic fields, energy density, longitudinal and transverse pressures, and other quantities.

arxiv-2101-11291.title: Which Nilpotent Groups are Self-Similar? Research supported by CNRS-UMR 5028 and Labex MILYON/ANR-10-LABX-0070.
arxiv-2101-11291.creator: Olivier Mathieu
arxiv-2101-11291.description: Abstract Let Γ \Gamma be a finitely generated torsion free nilpotent group, and let A ω A^{\omega} be the space of infinite words over a finite alphabet A A . We investigate two types of self-similar actions of Γ \Gamma on A ω A^{\omega} , namely the faithfull actions with dense orbits and the free actions.

arxiv-2406-07768.title: Selective Undercut of Undoped Optical Membranes for Spin-Active Color Centers in 4H-SiC
arxiv-2406-07768.description: Abstract . Silicon carbide (SiC) is a semiconductor used in quantum information processing, microelectromechanical systems, photonics, power electronics, and harsh environment sensors. However, its high temperature stability, high breakdown voltage, wide bandgap, and high mechanical strength are accompanied by a chemical inertness which makes complex micromachining difficult.

arxiv-2407-17355.title: Galois scaffolds for extraspecial p p -extensions in characteristic 0
arxiv-2407-17355.creator: Kevin Keating, Paul Schwartz
arxiv-2407-17355.description: Abstract Let K K be a local field of characteristic 0 with residue characteristic p p . Let G G be an extraspecial p p -group and let L / K L/K be a totally ramified G G -extension. In this paper we find sufficient conditions for L / K L/K to admit a Galois scaffold.

arxiv-2411-05036.title: From Word Vectors to Multimodal Embeddings: Techniques, Applications, and Future Directions For Large Language Models
arxiv-2411-05036.creator: Charles Zhang a, b , Benji Peng *, a, b , Xintian Sun c , Qian Niu d , Junyu Liu d , Keyu Chen a , Ming Li a , Pohsun Feng e , Ziqian Bi f , Ming Liu f , Yichao Zhang g , Xinyuan Song h , Cheng Fei i , Caitlyn Heqi Yin j , Lawrence KQ Yan k , Tianyang Wang l , Hongyang He m
arxiv-2411-05036.description: Abstract Word embeddings and language models have transformed natural language processing (NLP) by facilitating the representation of linguistic elements in continuous vector spaces. This review visits foundational concepts such as the distributional hypothesis and contextual similarity, tracing the evolution from sparse representations like one-hot encoding to dense embeddings including Word2Vec, GloVe, and fastText.

arxiv-2501-09074.title: Remarks on brane-antibrane inflation
arxiv-2501-09074.description: Abstract We provide an accessible review to the eta problem in brane-antibrane inflation and a recently proposed solution. The description of the antibrane by means of nonlinearly realized supersymmetry suggests a simple stabilization mechanism for the volume mode, based on the most general Kahler and superpotentials compatible with the symmetries of the problem.

arxiv-2504-12686.title: Rheology of dilute granular gases with hard-core and inverse power-law potentials
arxiv-2504-12686.creator: \firstname Yuria \lastname Kobayashi \fnsep, \firstname Shunsuke \lastname Iizuka, \firstname Satoshi \lastname Takada \fnsep
arxiv-2504-12686.description: Abstract The kinetic theory of dilute granular gases with hard-core and inverse power-law potentials is developed. The scattering process is studied theoretically, which yields the relative speed and the impact parameter dependence of the scattering angle. The viscosity is derived from the Boltzmann equation and its temperature dependence is plotted.

arxiv-2505-01063.title: Global controllability properties of linear control systems
arxiv-2505-01063.creator: Fritz Colonius, Alexandre J. Santana
arxiv-2505-01063.description: Abstract For linear control systems with bounded control range, the state space is compactified using the Poincaré sphere. The linearization of the induced control flow allows the construction of invariant manifolds on the sphere and of corresponding manifolds in the state space of the linear control system.

arxiv-2508-20306.title: Long-range spatial extension of exciton states in van der Waals heterostructure
arxiv-2508-20306.creator: Zhiwen Zhou, E. A. Szwed, W. J. Brunner, H. Henstridge, L. H. Fowler-Gerace, L. V. Butov
arxiv-2508-20306.description: Abstract Narrow lines in photoluminescence (PL) spectra of excitons are characteristic of low-dimensional semiconductors. These lines correspond to the emission of exciton states in local minima of a potential energy landscape formed by fluctuations of the local exciton environment in the heterostructure. The spatial extension of such states was in the nanometer range.

europmc-pmc7300008.title: Meta-analysis of the impacts of global change factors on soil microbial diversity and functionality.
europmc-pmc7300008.creator: Zhou Z, Wang C, Luo Y.
europmc-pmc7300008.description: Biodiversity on the Earth is changing at an unprecedented rate due to a variety of global change factors (GCFs). However, the effects of GCFs on microbial diversity is unclear despite that soil microorganisms play a critical role in biogeochemical cycling. Here, we synthesize...

pmc-10557324.title: Does tranexamic acid diminish hemorrhage and pain in open elbow arthrolysis? a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-10557324.creator: Mohammad Hadi Nejat, Amirhosein Khayami, Mahla Daliri, Mohammad H. Ebrahimzadeh, Masoumeh Sadeghi, Ali Moradi
pmc-10557324.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background/Objective: Effective hemostasis has the potential to reduce inflammation and pain, leading to potential benefits in the early rehabilitation of patients who undergo elbow arthrolysis. In the present study, we aim to assesse the effects of tranexamic acid (TXA) on elbow arthrolysis postoperative blood loss, patients’ pain perception according to the visual analog scale (VAS), elbow range of motion (ROM), and complications.MethodsWe systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, SCOPUS, and Cochrane Library.

pmc-10654838.title: Gait Analysis in Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus: A Meta‐Analysis
pmc-10654838.creator: Massimiliano Passaretti, Alessio Maranzano, Brent Bluett, Rajasumi Rajalingam, Alfonso Fasano
pmc-10654838.description: BackgroundGait analysis objectively quantifies gait impairment in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH), may improve diagnosis and evaluation for surgical candidacy.ObjectivesThis meta‐analysis aims to understand which objective gait parameters improve after tap‐test (TT) and CSF shunt surgery (CSS), also comparing responders (R) with non‐responders (NR) and to assess if gait restores within the range of healthy controls after procedures.

pmc-10671000.title: Protocol for a quasi-experimental study to ascertain the effectiveness of using eKnee School approach to impart self-care education to patients suffering from knee osteoarthritis during COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-10671000.creator: Meenakshi Sharma, Mandeep S. Dhillon, Amarjeet Singh, Shankar Prinja, Pankaj Bahuguna, Meenu Singh, Bibek Adhya, Sandeep Negi, Nishank Verma

Literature recommends nonpharmacological intervention as first-line treatment for KOA. The study aims to ascertain the effectiveness of online supervised nonpharmacological intervention sessions of virtual knee school (eKS) training among mild and moderate KOA patients in comparison to routine care during COVID-19 pandemic and assessment of cost-effectiveness of eKS against the routine care for KOA patients during COVID-19 pandemic.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A quasi-experimental pre-post with

pmc-11678547.title: Molecular Interaction Between Vasopressin and Insulin in Regulation of Metabolism: Impact on Cardiovascular and Metabolic Diseases
pmc-11678547.creator: Ewa Szczepanska-Sadowska, Agnieszka Cudnoch-Jędrzejewska, Tymoteusz Żera
pmc-11678547.description: Numerous compounds involved in the regulation of the cardiovascular system are also engaged in the control of metabolism. This review gives a survey of literature showing that arginine vasopressin (AVP), which is an effective cardiovascular peptide, exerts several direct and indirect metabolic effects and may play the role of the link adjusting blood supply to metabolism of tissues.

pmc-12645724.title: The Advocacy-Inquiry Rubric (AIR): a standard to build debriefing and feedback skills
pmc-12645724.creator: Clément Buléon, Demian Szyld, Robert Simon, Lon Setnik, Walter J. Eppich, Mary Fey, James A. Lipshaw, Janice C. Palaganas, Jenny W. Rudolph, Advocacy Inquiry Interest Group
pmc-12645724.description: BackgroundTeaching and learning debriefing and feedback skills—especially to a level of mastery—is challenging without an agreed-upon standard. There are a number of rating scales and rubrics to identify and evaluate debriefing and feedback skills that focus on an entire feedback or debriefing conversation.

pmc-12652386.title: “You’ve made it if you can, not have to live to survive, but live to live”: Beliefs about socioeconomic success and mobility among youth and parents in public housing
pmc-12652386.creator: Lindsay Lanteri, Jane Leer, Gabriella Valencia, Rebekah Levine Coley, Samantha Teixeira
pmc-12652386.description: Beliefs about success and social mobility are important contributors to young people’s wellbeing and motivation, yet understanding of youths’ and parents’ views on these factors is limited. Prior work is mostly quantitative, using researcher-defined definitions that prioritize financial success, educational attainment, and occupational prestige.

pmc-13116654.title: Epidemiology, Associated Factors and Implications for Effective Control of Pediculosis Among Primary Schoolgirls in Thailand: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13116654.creator: Manachai Yingklang, Patchana Hengboriboonpong Jaidee, Penchom Janwan, Wanchai Maleewong, Na T. D. Tran, Tongjit Thanchomnang
pmc-13116654.description: Simple SummaryPediculosis (head lice infestation) remains a persistent public health problem among primary schoolchildren in Thailand, particularly among schoolgirls. This study assessed the prevalence of pediculosis and explored associated factors across different socio-geographic regions and informed control strategies. A cross-sectional survey of 494 primary schoolgirls from eastern, northeastern, and southern provinces was conducted.

pmc-13246896.title: A content and quality analysis on open online platform videos on do not resuscitate (DNR)
pmc-13246896.creator: Elina Ahonen, Reino Pöyhiä, Minna Hökkä, Maria Valjus, Minna Peake, Eeva Pyörälä, Timo Carpén
pmc-13246896.description: The decision to implement a Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) order is a challenging medical decision made by physicians. Both laypersons and healthcare professionals need a better understanding of DNR orders. Educational videos could enhance DNR understanding, but their content and quality haven’t been systematically evaluated. A search on YouTube and Google identified 90 eligible videos for analysis.

pmc-13425952.title: Costs and health outcomes of liver transplantation for hepatocellular carcinoma: a scoping review
pmc-13425952.creator: Uriel Palacios-Barahona, Luis Guillermo Toro Rendón, Yuli Agudelo Berruecos, Angelica Fonseca, Diego Rojas-Gualdrón
pmc-13425952.description: BackgroundHepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver cancer, accounting for 70–90% of all cases. Liver transplantation has demonstrated superior survival rates compared to surgery; however, there is a significant knowledge gap regarding the costs and outcomes across different healthcare settings and patient populations.

pmc-13643987.title: Self-perception of occupational stigma among nurses – experience from Chinese nurses: a descriptive phenomenological research study
pmc-13643987.creator: Dexiu Yan, Yuzhen Zhou, Jian Chang, Yuanyuan Zhang, Lan Chen
pmc-13643987.description: ObjectiveThis research aims to understanding of nurses’ self-perceptions of professionalism and to explore their professional experiences in the workplace. It particularly focuses on the impact of occupational stigma—a key issue in nursing and mental health.BackgroundOccupational perceptions significantly influence nurses’ attitudes toward work. Understanding their professional experiences and social interactions is essential.
